title: Vinblastine and methotrexate for aggressive fibromatosis
purpose: Desmoid tumours do not spread to distant organs but can grow locally, cause pain and impair function. This treatment aims to control troublesome or progressive local disease and preserve daily function; it is not a metastatic-cancer survival treatment.
schedule_label: Vinblastine and methotrexate on days 1, 8 and 15; repeat every 28 days
schedule_summary: Vinblastine 6 mg/m² and methotrexate 30 mg/m² are given on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. Day 22 is a planned break. National Cancer Control Programme describes 12 cycles unless progression or unacceptable toxicity requires a change.
administration_text: Vinblastine is given intravenously over 10 minutes and methotrexate as an intravenous bolus by trained staff. Vinblastine is for intravenous use only. The appointment also includes safety review, prescribed support and observation.
monitoring_summary: Use the test-specific schedule below. Blood tests, organ checks and tumour-response assessments answer different questions.

agents.name: Vinblastine
agents.explanation: Vinblastine interferes with microtubules, preventing cells from dividing normally. Blood production, bowel movement and nerves may also be affected. It is given only into a vein by trained staff; other administration routes can be fatal.
agents.watch: Report fever, painful constipation with vomiting or abdominal swelling, new weakness or numbness, hearing changes and infusion-site pain promptly.
risks: Low blood counts with serious infection, anaemia or bleeding
Constipation, sometimes severe bowel slowing or blockage; mouth soreness, nausea and abdominal or jaw pain
Numbness, weakness and nerve injury; hearing or balance injury can occur and may persist
Hair loss, fatigue and fertility effects; severe tissue injury if the medicine leaks outside the vein
Allergic reactions and pregnancy harm; incorrect non-intravenous administration can be fatal

agents.name: Methotrexate
agents.explanation: Methotrexate interferes with folate-dependent processes needed to make genetic material and support cell growth. Mouth, bowel and blood cells can be affected. Reduced kidney clearance or fluid collections can prolong exposure and increase toxicity.
agents.watch: Report severe mouth ulcers or diarrhoea, dry cough or breathlessness, fever, yellow eyes, reduced urine or new neurological symptoms urgently. Ask the team before starting any medicine or supplement.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Mouth or bowel inflammation and ulceration; nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea can cause dehydration
Liver injury, including longer-term damage; kidney injury or accumulation when clearance is impaired
Lung inflammation can occur at this dose; a persistent dry cough or breathlessness requires urgent review
Rare severe skin or neurological effects and abnormal growth of immune cells (lymphoproliferative disorders); fertility and pregnancy harm
Serious medicine interactions, including with some antibiotics and painkillers; the injected oncology schedule is not a daily take-home dose
visual: Mouth, kidney, liver, blood and lung checks

anatomy: Methotrexate can cause ulcers. Report mouth sores, painful swallowing or severe diarrhoea before further treatment.
A new dry cough or breathlessness needs urgent assessment for infection or methotrexate-related lung inflammation.
Blood tests detect liver effects. Yellow eyes, dark urine or new significant upper abdominal pain needs prompt assessment.
Dehydration or kidney problems can raise methotrexate exposure. Report reduced urine, vomiting or difficulty drinking.
Low counts can cause infection, anaemia or bleeding. Fever, shaking chills or sudden illness needs immediate oncology contact.
Vinblastine can cause severe constipation. Pain, vomiting or abdominal swelling with constipation needs urgent advice.
Hair or skin changes can occur. Tell the nurse immediately about pain, burning or swelling where treatment enters the vein.
Report numbness, weakness, altered walking, hearing changes or balance problems before another vinblastine dose.

monitoring_schedule.note: Safety testing and tumour-response assessment have different purposes. Your plan may change after illness or a dose adjustment.

monitoring_test_details.label: Full blood count
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect low infection-fighting cells, anaemia and bleeding risk.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and before each cycle as specified by National Cancer Control Programme. The team also reviews current blood counts before each planned dose, including days 8 and 15, and confirms when samples are needed; count recovery is required before further vinblastine.

monitoring_test_details.label: Kidney function and hydration
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Identify reduced methotrexate clearance and prevent accumulation.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and before each cycle; sooner for dehydration, reduced urine, vomiting, diarrhoea or new fluid collections.

monitoring_test_details.label: Liver tests
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess safe dosing and identify liver injury.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and before each cycle; repeat sooner for abnormal results or symptoms. Drug-specific source and product thresholds must be reconciled.

monitoring_test_details.label: Chest and breathing assessment
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Record baseline lung status and detect infection or drug-related inflammation.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Chest X-ray before treatment. Investigate a new dry cough or breathlessness promptly; routine repeated X-rays are not specified.

monitoring_test_details.label: Mouth and bowel review
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect methotrexate-related ulcers and vinblastine-related constipation.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Review before further dosing and report new symptoms between visits. Severe pain, vomiting, abdominal swelling or inability to drink needs urgent advice.

monitoring_test_details.label: Nerves, hearing and balance
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect effects that may require vinblastine review.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Ask about numbness, weakness, hearing changes or balance problems before further treatment and whenever symptoms change.

monitoring_test_details.label: Tumour response, symptoms and function
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess benefit separately from safety blood tests.
monitoring_test_details.timing: The specialist sets scan and clinical-review timing for the tumour type, treatment aim and symptoms.

support.title: Preparation and support medicines
support.text: Ask oncology/pharmacy before taking anti-inflammatory painkillers, trimethoprim or co-trimoxazole, other antibiotics, proton-pump inhibitors, folate supplements or new medicines. Avoid alcohol. Tell anaesthesia staff about methotrexate before procedures, including possible nitrous oxide use. Do not self-stop essential medicines; have the complete list reconciled. Methotrexate has low and vinblastine minimal nausea/vomiting risk. National Cancer Control Programme lists no usual separate premedication or routine additional prophylaxis. Use individual anti-sickness, mouth and constipation support. The team prescribes any rescue medicines, extra hydration or white-cell growth-factor injections individually; the separate high-dose methotrexate support programme does not automatically apply.

support.title: Access and practical care
support.text: The team chooses appropriate intravenous access and explains its care. Report pain, burning, redness or swelling during treatment immediately. If a port or peripherally inserted central catheter is used, confirm dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements.

support.title: Fertility and pregnancy precautions
support.text: Discuss fertility preservation before treatment. Avoid pregnancy and obtain written contraception and breastfeeding instructions for every medicine, including how long precautions continue after the last dose. Do not assume all drugs have the same waiting period. Contact oncology promptly if pregnancy is possible.

support.title: Your wider treatment plan
support.text: A specialist desmoid team weighs observation, systemic options, selected local treatment, symptoms, tumour location and function. Some desmoid tumours can stabilise without immediate treatment. Surgery and radiotherapy are individual decisions because local treatment can itself affect function. Discuss pain management, rehabilitation and psychological support alongside tumour control.

support.title: Skin protection, vaccines and procedures
support.text: Use sun protection and report a blistering rash urgently. Ask oncology before vaccination, new medicines or procedures; do not take folate or rescue medicines without a specific prescription.

items.title: General chemotherapy risks
items.text: Discuss low blood counts with serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding; nausea or vomiting; mouth soreness, appetite or taste changes, diarrhoea or constipation; fatigue, hair, nail and skin changes; changes in sexual wellbeing; allergic reactions and intravenous-line complications; blood clots, including clots in the legs or lungs; fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding effects; and the possibility of lasting organ injury, rare later cancers or death from serious treatment complications. The likelihood and severity differ between medicines and people. Use this general discussion together with every medicine-specific risk below.

evidence.title: Methotrexate and vinblastine in advanced aggressive fibromatosis
evidence.summary: A small historical phase II study using methotrexate 30 mg/m² and vinblastine 6 mg/m² weekly found tumour shrinkage or stability and symptom benefit in some patients with advanced inoperable aggressive fibromatosis. It supports activity but had no randomised comparator.
evidence.intro: A small historical phase II study using methotrexate 30 mg/m² and vinblastine 6 mg/m² weekly found tumour shrinkage or stability and symptom benefit in some patients with advanced inoperable aggressive fibromatosis. It supports activity but had no randomised comparator.
evidence.caveat: The study used continuous weekly treatment, rather than the current National Cancer Control Programme days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle. DESMOPAZ used vinblastine 5 mg/m² and a different weekly-then-fortnightly schedule; its non-comparative randomised design does not establish a definitive head-to-head superiority result. Do not present trial rates as validated estimates for this exact schedule.

questions.q: What is the treatment trying to do?
questions.a: Desmoid tumours do not spread to distant organs but can grow locally, cause pain and impair function. This treatment aims to control troublesome or progressive local disease and preserve daily function; it is not a metastatic-cancer survival treatment. A specialist desmoid team weighs observation, systemic options, selected local treatment, symptoms, tumour location and function. Some desmoid tumours can stabilise without immediate treatment. Surgery and radiotherapy are individual decisions because local treatment can itself affect function. Discuss pain management, rehabilitation and psychological support alongside tumour control.

Vinblastine 6 mg/m² and methotrexate 30 mg/m² are given on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. Day 22 is a planned break. National Cancer Control Programme describes 12 cycles unless progression or unacceptable toxicity requires a change.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.

questions.q: Can I restart after a delay or safety hold?
questions.a: Only after the treating team gives an explicit plan. A normal result does not erase a previous severe reaction or permanent-stop decision.

questions.q: Are safety tests the same as checking benefit?
questions.a: No. Safety tests look for treatment effects on the body. Scans, symptoms and function help the specialist assess tumour control.
